title: Factorization of a polynomial with constant term one into linear factors $1-\alpha_jT$ over an algebraically closed field
statement:
Let $K$ be a field, $T$ an indeterminate, and let $L$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-algebraic-closure] together with a ring homomorphism $\iota:K\to L$ (for instance $K=\Ql$ and $L=\Qlb$ an algebraic closure of $\Ql$). Let $P(T)\in K[T]$ [def-weil-polynomial-ring] satisfy $P(0)=1$, and put $r=\deg P\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$. Write $P_L\in L[T]$ for the polynomial obtained by applying $\iota$ to the coefficients of $P$, so that $P(x)=P_L(x)$ for $x\in L$ [def-weil-polynomial-root]. Then:

1. Every root $\beta\in L$ of $P$ is nonzero. Hence $\beta\mapsto\beta^{-1}$ is a bijection from the set of roots of $P$ in $L$ onto the set of *reciprocal roots* of $P$ in $L$, the elements $\alpha\in L^\times$ with $P(\alpha^{-1})=0$.

2. There exist $\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_r\in L^\times$ such that, in $L[T]$,

$$
P_L(T)=\prod_{j=1}^{r}(1-\alpha_jT).
$$

3. The family $(\alpha_j)_{1\leq j\leq r}$ is unique up to reordering: for every $\alpha\in L^\times$ the number of indices $j$ with $\alpha_j=\alpha$ equals $m_{\alpha^{-1}}(P_L)$, the multiplicity of $\alpha^{-1}$ as a root of $P_L$ [def-weil-root-multiplicity], which is also the multiplicity $m_\alpha(P_L^\#)$ of $\alpha$ as a root of the reciprocal polynomial $P_L^\#(U)=U^rP_L(U^{-1})$ [lem-weil-reciprocal-polynomial]. In particular the $\alpha_j$ are exactly the reciprocal roots of $P$ in $L$, each occurring $m_{\alpha_j^{-1}}(P_L)$ times (its *algebraic multiplicity* as a reciprocal root), and the number of reciprocal roots counted with multiplicity is $r=\deg P$.

proof.text: Setup. A ring homomorphism $\iota:K\to L$ between fields is injective: if $x\neq0$ and $\iota(x)=0$ then $1=\iota(x x^{-1})=\iota(x)\iota(x^{-1})=0$ in $L$, impossible. Hence, by [lem-weil-coefficientwise-extension-degree], $P_L$ has degree $\deg P_L=\deg P=r$, its coefficient of $T^m$ is $\iota([T^m]P)$, and $P_L(0)=\iota(P(0))=\iota(1)=1$. In particular $P_L\neq0$, and for $x\in L$ the value $P(x)$ of [def-weil-polynomial-root] equals $P_L(x)$.

source.place: written by an agent (standard algebra; WANTED: S. Lang, Algebra, Ch. IV §1, roots and their multiplicities, factorization over an algebraically closed field)

proof.text: Clause 1. If $\beta\in L$ is a root of $P$, then $\beta\neq0$, because $P(0)=P_L(0)=1\neq0$ (step 1). So $\beta\mapsto\beta^{-1}$ is defined on the roots; it sends a root $\beta$ to $\alpha=\beta^{-1}\in L^\times$ with $P(\alpha^{-1})=P(\beta)=0$, a reciprocal root, and $\alpha\mapsto\alpha^{-1}$ is its inverse map, since inversion is an involution of $L^\times$.

source.place: written by an agent (standard algebra; WANTED: S. Lang, Algebra, Ch. IV §1, roots and their multiplicities, factorization over an algebraically closed field)

proof.text: Linear factorization of $P_L$. Since $L$ is algebraically closed and $P_L\neq0$ (step 1), [lem-weil-alg-closed-linear-factorization] gives $n\geq0$, $\beta_1,\dots,\beta_n\in L$ and $c\in L^\times$ with $P_L(T)=c\prod_{i=1}^n(T-\beta_i)$. Comparing degrees ($\deg$ of a product of $n$ monic linear factors times a nonzero constant is $n$, as $L$ is a field), $n=\deg P_L=r$. Each $\beta_i$ is a root of $P_L$ (the factor $T-\beta_i$ vanishes at $\beta_i$ and evaluation at $\beta_i$ is a ring homomorphism), so $\beta_i\neq0$ by step 2.

source.place: written by an agent (standard algebra; WANTED: S. Lang, Algebra, Ch. IV §1, roots and their multiplicities, factorization over an algebraically closed field)

proof.text: Clause 2. Put $\alpha_i=\beta_i^{-1}\in L^\times$ ($1\le i\le r$). In $L[T]$, $T-\beta_i=-\beta_i(1-\alpha_iT)$, so $P_L(T)=c\prod_{i=1}^r(-\beta_i)\cdot\prod_{i=1}^r(1-\alpha_iT)$. Evaluating at $T=0$ (a ring homomorphism $L[T]\to L$) gives $1=P_L(0)=c\prod_i(-\beta_i)\cdot1$. Hence $P_L(T)=\prod_{i=1}^r(1-\alpha_iT)$ with all $\alpha_i\in L^\times$.

source.place: written by an agent (standard algebra; WANTED: S. Lang, Algebra, Ch. IV §1, roots and their multiplicities, factorization over an algebraically closed field)

proof.text: Multiplicities of the roots of $P_L$. Let $(\alpha_j)_{1\le j\le r}$ be any family in $L^\times$ with $P_L=\prod_{j=1}^r(1-\alpha_jT)$ (for instance the one of step 4). Since $1-\alpha_jT=-\alpha_j(T-\alpha_j^{-1})$, $P_L=u\prod_{j=1}^r(T-\alpha_j^{-1})$ with $u=\prod_j(-\alpha_j)\in L^\times$. Let $\gamma\in L$. All factors are nonzero, so by [lem-weil-root-multiplicity-mul] (applied $r$ times) $m_\gamma(P_L)=m_\gamma(u)+\sum_{j=1}^rm_\gamma(T-\alpha_j^{-1})$. By [lem-weil-root-multiplicity-pos-iff], $m_\gamma(u)=0$ (the constant $u\neq0$ does not vanish at $\gamma$) and $m_\gamma(T-\delta)=0$ for $\delta\neq\gamma$; and $m_\gamma(T-\gamma)=1$ by [def-weil-root-multiplicity], since $(T-\gamma)^1$ divides $T-\gamma$ while $(T-\gamma)^2$, of degree $2$, does not divide the nonzero polynomial $T-\gamma$ of degree $1$. Hence $m_\gamma(P_L)=\#\{j:\alpha_j^{-1}=\gamma\}$, and for $\alpha\in L^\times$, taking $\gamma=\alpha^{-1}$: $\#\{j:\alpha_j=\alpha\}=m_{\alpha^{-1}}(P_L)$.

source.place: written by an agent (standard algebra; WANTED: S. Lang, Algebra, Ch. IV §1, roots and their multiplicities, factorization over an algebraically closed field)

proof.text: Multiplicities as roots of $P_L^\#$. By step 1, $P_L\in L[T]$ has constant coefficient $1$ and degree $r$ (nonzero coefficient of $T^r$), so its reciprocal polynomial $P_L^\#(U)=\sum_{k=0}^r[T^k]P_L\,U^{r-k}$ is defined [lem-weil-reciprocal-polynomial]; in the notation of [lem-weil-polynomial-reflection-multiplicative] it is $\mathrm{rev}_r(P_L)$. For the family of step 5, each factor $1-\alpha_jT$ has degree $\le1$ and $\mathrm{rev}_1(1-\alpha_jT)=U-\alpha_j$ (coefficients $1,-\alpha_j$ read backwards), so by [lem-weil-polynomial-reflection-multiplicative] $P_L^\#=\mathrm{rev}_{1+\dots+1}\bigl(\prod_{j=1}^r(1-\alpha_jT)\bigr)=\prod_{j=1}^r(U-\alpha_j)$. Applying the computation of step 5 to this product (with $u=1$, [lem-weil-root-multiplicity-mul], [lem-weil-root-multiplicity-pos-iff], [def-weil-root-multiplicity]) gives $m_\alpha(P_L^\#)=\#\{j:\alpha_j=\alpha\}=m_{\alpha^{-1}}(P_L)$ for every $\alpha\in L^\times$.

source.place: written by an agent (standard algebra; WANTED: S. Lang, Algebra, Ch. IV §1, roots and their multiplicities, factorization over an algebraically closed field)

proof.text: Clause 3, uniqueness and the 'in particular'. Two families $(\alpha_j)$, $(\alpha'_j)$ in $L^\times$ satisfying clause 2 have, by step 5, the same number $m_{\alpha^{-1}}(P_L)$ of indices with value $\alpha$ for every $\alpha\in L^\times$, so one is a reordering of the other. An element $\alpha\in L^\times$ occurs among the $\alpha_j$ iff $m_{\alpha^{-1}}(P_L)\geq1$, iff $P_L(\alpha^{-1})=0$ by [lem-weil-root-multiplicity-pos-iff] ($P_L\neq0$), i.e. iff $\alpha$ is a reciprocal root of $P$ (step 1: $P(\alpha^{-1})=P_L(\alpha^{-1})$); it occurs $m_{\alpha^{-1}}(P_L)$ times, and summing these counts over the distinct values gives the length $r=\deg P$ of the family.

Added def-weil-field and def-weil-polynomial-coefficient to stmt_deps (L^x, degree). Statement unchanged; checked the edge case r = 0 (P = 1, empty product).
